blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Online scene change detection requires integrating incoming observations to determine which regions have changed relative to a reference scene. We update change beliefs as new images arrive using generalised Bayesian evidence fusion. However, the prior probability of change and evidence models are unknown beforehand, and numerical Bayesian inference can be costly. We address these challenges by learning offline from automatic edits to a reference 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model. These edits generate labelled training views without manual annotations. Together with unchanged reference observations, they provide supervision for learning scene-specific evidence models and estimating the effective pixel prior and response statistics. Online prediction combines current evidence with historical support, while closed-form local Bayes factors, parameterized by the learned response statistics, update an accumulated 3D Gaussian field. Object-guided refinement produces the final change masks. Our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on PASLCD and CCS3D, with $67.64\%$ and $75.82\%$ mIoU, respectively. On PASLCD, the complete pipeline runs at $17.2$\,FPS over complete query sequences, the fastest among the evaluated online methods.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Scene change detection identifies physical changes in an environment from images captured at different times.
When captures follow different camera trajectories, viewpoint and visibility differences complicate direct image comparison ( Lu et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2026 ) .
A reference 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) enables rendering the earlier scene at query viewpoints, providing a common view for comparison.
Recent methods, such as MV3DCD ( Galappaththige et al., 2025 ) and O-SCD ( Galappaththige et al., 2026b ) , integrate multi-view change cues by optimizing per-Gaussian change parameters, using batch and online processing, respectively.
blocks.zh:
场景变化探测从不同时间捕获的图像中识别出环境中的物理变化.
当捕获遵循不同的相机轨迹时,视角和能见度的差异使直接图像比较复杂化(Lu等人,2025年;Wu等人,2026年).
一个参考的3D Gaussian Splateting(3DGS)模型(Kerbl et al., 2023)可以使更早的场景在查询角度上渲染,为比较提供了共同的观点.
近代方法如MV3DCD(Galappaththige et al.,2025)和O-SCD(Galappaththige et al.,2026b),通过优化每古西语变化参数,分别使用批量和在线处理,整合多视图变化提示.

blocks.en:
In O-SCD, processing each new image requires iterative optimization using current and replayed observations, adding computational overhead during online inference.
However, updating predictions as new evidence arrives does not inherently require repeated parameter optimization.
This motivates updating change beliefs as new images arrive. Generalised Bayesian inference ( Bissiri et al., 2016 ) provides a framework to combine a prior probability of change with incoming evidence.
blocks.zh:
在O-SCD中,每个新图像的处理都需要利用当前和重播的观测数据进行迭代优化,在在线推导时增加计算间接费用.
然而,随着新证据的到来而更新预测,本质上不需要重复参数优化.
这激励着随着新图像的到来而更新改变信仰. 一般的贝叶斯推论(Bissiri等人,2016年)提供了一个框架,将先前的改变概率与收到的证据结合起来.

blocks.en:
Putting this idea into practice requires a prior and models that translate image differences into change evidence, which are unknown beforehand.
We estimate these quantities offline using automatic reference 3DGS edits and unchanged observations.
The edits turn the reference representation into a source of labelled training views, supporting scene-specific learning without manual change annotations.
This reduces dependence on large labelled datasets for training a single evidence model across diverse scene appearances and changes.
The learned evidence models also support efficient Bayesian evidence accumulation.
Evaluating Bayesian evidence can require numerical integration or sampling ( Kass & Raftery, 1995 ) , adding substantial cost when repeated for incoming frames.
We apply the learned evidence models to unchanged reference observations to estimate response statistics, which parameterize a local Bayesian model that admits closed-form Bayes factors.
We combine current evidence with historical support for prediction and use these Bayes factors to update the accumulated field for subsequent queries.
These updates require neither online backpropagation nor past-image replay.
Finally, object-guided refinement sharpens boundaries and completes missed object regions.

Our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on PASLCD and CCS3D, with 67.64 % 67.64\% and 75.82 % 75.82\% mIoU, respectively.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Scene change detection. Image-pair methods identify changes through correspondence and appearance comparison.
GeSCF uses SAM features and mask matching without task-specific training ( Kim & Kim, 2025 ) , while SceneDiff compares objects across before–after captures using semantic and geometric information ( Wu et al., 2026 ) .
A reference 3D representation additionally enables comparisons at matched viewpoints and integration across observations.
3DGS-CD associates image-level detections across views ( Lu et al., 2025 ) , and SCaR-3D combines change cues through multi-view voting and pruning ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) .
MV3DCD optimizes Gaussian change channels from a collection of post-change images ( Galappaththige et al., 2025 ) ; O-SCD extends this approach to streaming queries, updating change parameters using current and replayed observations ( Galappaththige et al., 2026b ) .
CL-Splats uses detected changes to guide local updates of a Gaussian scene representation ( Ackermann et al., 2025 ) .
GS-Diff instead compares geometry and colour between independently reconstructed scene states ( Galappaththige et al., 2026a ) .
Our method accumulates evidence on the reference Gaussians without online optimization or past-image replay.

blocks.en:
Learning from synthetic changes and 3D editing. CYWS constructs training pairs from object segmentation data ( Sachdeva & Zisserman, 2023a ) , while CYWS-3D generates paired observations from synthetic 3D scenes ( Sachdeva & Zisserman, 2023b ) .
Both use synthetic supervision to train change detectors that generalize to unseen scenes, requiring training data to cover diverse scene appearances and changes.
Advances in 3DGS segmentation ( Ye et al., 2024 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) , editing ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Lee et al., 2025 ) , and relighting ( Liang et al., 2024 ; Gao et al., 2024 ) enable controlled scene modifications.
RoboSplat edits Gaussian scenes and varies their appearance to train robot policies ( Yang et al., 2025 ) , while Zanjani et al. (2025) insert Gaussian objects into driving scenes to train 3D detectors.
Given a prebuilt reference 3DGS and its associated unchanged observations, we generate labelled changes through automatic edits and fit scene-specific evidence models and a prior offline.
This allows learning to focus on the appearance and response statistics of each reference scene, rather than requiring a single evidence model to cover many different environments.

blocks.en:
Bayesian evidence accumulation. Bayesian updates provide a way to combine successive observations with existing beliefs.
In scene mapping, POCD updates probabilistic object states using geometric and semantic information to track changes and maintain volumetric maps ( Qian et al., 2022 ) . Bissiri et al. (2016) provide a generalised Bayesian framework that connects observations to belief updates through a loss function.
For online time-series changepoint detection, Altamirano et al. (2023) construct generalised Bayesian updates with closed-form posterior parameters using diffusion score matching.
We apply generalised Bayesian prediction to scene change detection, using offline-learned response statistics to evaluate local Bayes factors in closed form for accumulation on reference Gaussians.

对于在线时间序列的变点检测,Altamirano等人(2023年)利用扩散分数匹配,用闭式后置参数构建了泛泛的巴耶西亚语更新.

Automatic reference editing. We split reference cameras approximately 5 : 1 5{:}1 into an editing subset for learning and an unchanged-only subset for estimating unchanged-response statistics. A regular grid of automatic point prompts drives the SAM2 mask decoder ( Ravi et al., 2025 ) on reference views, and masks are matched across views through their contributing Gaussians. Aggregating matched masks X X via [ 𝒜 t ​ ( X ) ] g [\mathcal{A}_{t}(X)]_{g} (Eq. 3 ) yields object membership m g ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] m_{g}\in[0,1] , measuring the fraction of each Gaussian’s rendering footprint inside the object. We select objects based on their consistency across held-out views. Recolouring blends colours towards the palette colour furthest from the object’s median colour with mixing coefficient 0.45 ​ m g 0.45m_{g} ; removal scales opacity by 1 − m g 1-m_{g} ; translation applies a shared 3D displacement to Gaussians with m g ≥ 0.5 m_{g}\geq 0.5 . Edits modify duplicate models, preserving the original reference.

We introduce lighting variations using affine colour transforms, optionally augmented with normal-dependent directional shading, fitted to differences between unchanged reference images and their renderings. These transformations preserve the change labels (details and additional examples in Appendix A.1 , Figure 4 ).

blocks.en: Protocol. Real-world PASLCD ( Galappaththige et al., 2025 ) is our primary benchmark (20 scene-instances, conventional 4 × 4\times downsampling), complemented by evaluation on four synthetic CCS3D scenes ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) . Following O-SCD’s mask definition, we evaluate our method and O-SCD on both datasets using masks covering pre- and post-state changes, including vacated and newly occupied regions. Tables 2 – 2 compare our method with official-code O-SCD results and other published online/offline baselines. blocks.en: 6 Conclusion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 6. 结论和限制

blocks.en:
Our method learns scene-specific evidence models and statistics from automatic
reference 3DGS edits, using the reference scene as a source of supervision for
online change detection. These learned quantities enable closed-form local
Bayes factors and generalised Bayesian history accumulation without online
backpropagation or past-image replay. It outperforms O-SCD on PASLCD and CCS3D,
achieving 67.64 % 67.64\% mIoU at 17.2 17.2 FPS on PASLCD.
However, our direct object edits and simple relighting prioritize short offline
preparation and may not cover real changes or unusual lighting conditions.
Accumulating evidence on the unchanged reference geometry limits how accurately
newly introduced objects and occlusion boundaries can be represented in the field.
The response uncertainty and spatial covariance models are working approximations.
Although local Bayes factors are evaluated analytically under the residual model,
the fused scores combine dependent evidence and are not guaranteed to be
calibrated probabilities of real-world changes.
Future work will explore more advanced 3DGS segmentation, editing, and relighting
to improve object masks and broaden the generated changes, while assessing whether
the resulting detection gains justify the additional offline preparation time.

To exploit view continuity in sequentially captured reference images,
we match each view with the next K K views in the reference sequence.
This reduces pairwise comparisons while allowing matches to be linked
through intermediate views into longer tracks. We use K = 2 K=2 .
We match masks across views by comparing the Gaussians assigned to them.
For each candidate pair, we use a hypergeometric test to determine
whether the two masks share more Gaussians than expected by chance.
The test accounts for both support-set sizes and uses all Gaussians
visible in either view, 𝒱 t ∪ 𝒱 l \mathcal{V}_{t}\cup\mathcal{V}_{l} , as the population. We apply the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure ( Benjamini & Hochberg, 1995 ) at level 0.01 0.01 to filter chance overlaps across the candidate pairs.
Among the surviving pairs, we rank matches by Jaccard overlap
(intersection size divided by union size), breaking ties by the number
of shared Gaussians. We retain a pair only if each mask is the other’s
highest-ranked match in the corresponding view. Finally, we link these matches into cross-view tracks, where each track is a
collection of masks associated with the same candidate object across
reference views, with at most one mask per view.

blocks.en: Continuous sequence timing. After initialization, synchronized wall-clock timing starts before the first query is retrieved and ends when the final mask is ready. Input prefetching starts during initialization for both methods; remaining input waits and all inter-frame work are included. O-SCD also waits for GPU work to complete at its stage synchronization points; these waits are included in the timed sequence. Mask export and metric evaluation occur outside timing. FPS is the total number of processed frames divided by summed sequence duration: 1,000 frames across two runs for each of our output modes and 500 frames for O-SCD(O). The pixel runs achieve 27.88 27.88 and 27.98 27.98 FPS; the full runs achieve 17.15 17.15 and 17.19 17.19 FPS.
blocks.zh: 连续的顺序时间。 初始化后,同步的墙钟计时在第一个查询被检索之前开始,最后的面具准备好后结束. 两种方法在初始化期间开始输入预缩写;剩余输入等待和所有框架间工作都包括在内. O-SCD也等待GPU工作在其阶段同步点完成;这些等待被包含在定时序列中. 遮罩输出和度量评价发生在时间之外。 FPS是经过处理的帧总数,除以总和的序列持续时间:我们每个输出模式的1000帧跨2个运行,O-SCD(O)的500帧. 像素运行实现27.88 27.88和27.98 FPS;全程实现17.15 17.15和17.19 17.19 FPS.

blocks.en: Batch refinement timing. O-SCD(R) first processes the query images sequentially, then jointly refines its change representation using all views and renders the final masks. Its timing covers this complete procedure, from the first input retrieval to the last refined mask, excluding initialization and file export. We divide total sequence time by the number of frames for Table 4 ; the resulting per-frame time and equivalent FPS describe batch processing, not online prediction latency. Over the same 20 instances, complete processing averages 5.03 5.03 s per 25-frame sequence, including 3.29 3.29 s of post-sequence optimization and 6.48 6.48 ms of final mask rendering.
blocks.zh: 批量完善时机. O-SCD(R)首先按顺序处理查询图像,然后利用所有视图共同完善其变化表示,并制作最终的口罩. 它的时间涵盖了这一完整的程序,从第一次输入检索到最后一次精制的面具,不包括初始化和文件导出. 将总序列时间除以表4的帧数;产生的每帧时间和等效的FPS描述批处理,而不是在线预测延迟. 在同样的20个案例中,完整的处理平均为每25帧5.03秒5.03秒,包括3.29秒的序列后优化和6.48公分的终极面具渲染.

blocks.en: Initialization. Initialization comprises loading scene and model parameters, preparing reference matching data, and pre-executing model and GPU operations using non-test inputs. Both methods run SAM on all-zero inputs. Our method additionally processes a fixed reference-edit observation twice through the complete detection pipeline, using synthetic data already available from offline editing. We then restore the detector history, reference matching state, and random-generator states before processing the query sequence. Initialization averages 14.08 14.08 s for our pixel pipeline, 15.54 15.54 s for our full pipeline, and 7.16 7.16 s for O-SCD(O). The two reference-edit passes take 0.111 0.111 and 0.168 0.168 s for the pixel and full pipelines. Mean first-frame latency is 35.55 35.55 , 58.24 58.24 , and 110.38 110.38 ms, respectively.
blocks.zh: 初释. 初始化包括加载场景和模型参数,编写参考匹配数据,以及使用非测试输入的预执行模型和GPU操作. 两种方法都在全零输入上运行 SAM. 我们的方法还利用离线编辑中已有的合成数据,通过完整的检测管道两次处理固定的参考编辑观测。 然后在处理查询序列之前恢复探测器历史,参考匹配状态,以及随机生成状态. 我国象素管线的初始化平均为14.08 14.08s,全线15.54 15.54s,O-SCD(O)7.16 7.16s. 两次参考编辑的通行证需要0.110.11和0.1680.168s的像素和全管. 平均第一帧延迟分别为35.55 35.55、58.24 58.24和110.38 110.38毫秒。

blocks.en: Stage-wise timing. The frontend comprises query relocalisation, reference rendering, and initial change-cue computation (Section 3 ). Post-frontend time covers detection, temporal-state updates, and refinement where applicable. Table 11 averages synchronized profiles over all 25 frames of all 20 instances. Detection includes the pixel decision and history update; refinement includes its RGB transfer. Input waits and inter-frame work are reported separately. Our profiles use a separate pass from the continuous throughput measurements in Table 4 ; O-SCD(O) uses its synchronized sequence records.

blocks.en: G.6 Offline Preparation and Component Timing Breakdown
blocks.zh: G.6 离线准备和组件时间安排

blocks.en: Offline preparation includes fitting the pixel prior and contour filter from reference edits.
blocks.zh: 离线准备包括从参考编辑中安装像素前置和轮廓过滤器。

blocks.en:
Table 12 details the offline preparation and component fitting time across all 20 PASLCD scene-instances, measured on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 using wall-clock timing with GPU synchronization.
The offline workflow comprises two main phases: (1) synthetic edit generation , which extracts multi-view object proposals with SAM2, performs 3D Gaussian edits (recolouring, removal, translation), renders lighting-varied views, and forms training observation pairs; and (2) scene component fitting , which executes reference preprocessing, fits the pixel pipeline components (response suppression, log-likelihood ratio mapping, unchanged response moments, and 1D branch-and-bound prior search π ⋆ \pi^{\star} ), and trains the 18-dimensional symmetric contour filter with Platt scaling.
Across all instances, the complete offline workflow averages 215.82 215.82 s ( ∼ \sim 3.6 minutes; median 197.13 197.13 s, ranging from 142.15 142.15 s to 440.69 440.69 s), given an existing reference reconstruction.
